author: Edge
text: A lot of my friends here probably already know this. But for the few starting out, understanding the micro structure of the FL can be interesting. The building blocks of price are fascinating. In the body area of the FL there can also be nested orders. The IT algos, push for a average best price within an acceptable range. That's why sometimes the mpl/apex is left for future use.

text:
staurum wrote:

Edge, any words of wisdom?

As K mentions the MPL is the best area, but its not the only area. For me I dont like the nested orders in the body. I would only ever use the mouth or body orders to go to a lower scale, or as TGs on that scale where I would hope for the MPL on that lower scale and wait for appropriate PA. If I was not drilling down, I would prefer to miss trades because I love the MPL.

If we enter on the absolute best levels and are aware of even the conservative TGs the number of trades we take may drop however, the R and win rate will be better.

Hi Edge, I enjoy thinking about these things too, so thought I would chime in - even though my experience with this is still in it's infancy.. who doesn't like a good poll?

My thoughts coincide with 2) - "we don't actually know which set of orders in the flag limit may turn price. It could either be the mouth, body or MPL".

Of course as is mentioned the MPL is absolutely the best trade, and I mostly prefer to wait for these orders as well, but we have no guarantees that price will reach the last remaining orders there. If I am to take a trade at the mouth of a FL, it will depend on the size of the FL; with good space provided by PA to allow a trade down to a first target, and a tight FL, we have the luxury of a smaller stop loss, - since whatever the scenario, one thing is certain, my stop must go above the FL we're reacting to. For larger FLs, I'd much rather wait for the MPL of the FL. This is mainly for trade management, and keeping my stops tighter. With nothing to the left, I don't yet see a reason why we can assume that price will necessarily want the MPL, when the ITs may well have all their orders filled by the time price hits the kink to the mouth of the FL, or any possible free pockets of liquidity in the body on the way to the MPL..

This is where I am at with my thinking on this, and of course welcome more thoughts and opinions to build a solid framework for all of this!
